articles.title: 🍎 Apple Gets A New CEO; He Inherits The Company, The Cash, And The Unfinished Homework Called 'Apple Intelligence'
articles.dateline: CUPERTINO — reported from a freshly reupholstered chair
paras: Apple installed a new chief executive this week, handing him the keys to the most valuable gadget empire on Earth along with its trickiest open question: what, exactly, is the plan for the company's much-discussed, much-delayed AI push.

"We're excited for the next chapter," the company said, of a leadership handoff that comes with a corner office, a stock chart shaped like a mountain, and a to-do list whose first item is "figure out the AI thing everyone keeps asking about." Analysts note the new boss inherits a machine that prints money and a mandate to make the voice assistant, at long last, unembarrassing.

articles.title: ⚡ A.I. Startup's New Cash Will Buy A Full Gigawatt Of Computing; The Company Now Requires Its Own Power Plant
articles.dateline: SHENZHEN — reported beside a humming substation
paras: An AI company's fresh multibillion-dollar war chest will reportedly fund roughly a gigawatt of new computing capacity — an amount of power that has quietly promoted the startup from "software company" to "entity that must now think seriously about electricity."

"Scale is everything," executives said, of a plan to acquire enough compute to run a small city's worth of thinking. Analysts note the defining unit of the AI age is no longer the algorithm but the gigawatt, and that every ambitious lab now dreams less of a breakthrough and more of a very large, very reliable extension cord.

articles.title: 🆓 Free A.I. Models Quietly Catch Up To The Expensive Ones; Paid Labs Discover The Terror Of 'Good Enough, For Nothing'
articles.dateline: THE REPO — reported from a suspiciously affordable download
paras: Open-source AI models are rapidly closing the gap with pricey commercial ones, meaning the free option is now nearly as good as the expensive one — a development thrilling for everyone except the companies whose entire business is that shrinking difference.

"Premium still offers more," paid labs insist, in the strained voice of a restaurant explaining why its water costs money now that the tap works fine. Experts note that "nearly as good, but completely free" are the most dangerous words in commerce, and the AI industry may be about to learn what the encyclopedia and the newspaper already know.

articles.title: 🤖 Humanoid Robots Start Taking Real Jobs; A Machine Now Greets You At The Store And Means It More Than The Last Guy
articles.dateline: THE SHOP FLOOR — reported near aisle 4
paras: With humanoid robots getting cheaper and more capable, companies are quietly slotting them into actual roles — greeting, stocking, serving — meaning the friendly face welcoming you to the store may now run on batteries and boundless, uncomplaining enthusiasm.

"They're wonderful with customers," a manager said, of employees who never call in sick, never roll their eyes, and never quietly resent a schedule they cannot express. Sociologists note the robots are polite, efficient, and unsettlingly consistent — which is either excellent customer service or the single most ominous thing a store greeter has ever been.

articles.title: 🔁 A.I. Now Writes The Job Applications And Also Screens Them; Two Robots Negotiate Your Career While You Wait Outside
articles.dateline: THE HR DEPARTMENT — reported from the waiting room
paras: As AI tools flood hiring, candidates now use AI to write their résumés and cover letters while companies use AI to read and rank them — producing the perfectly modern job hunt, in which two machines correspond at length about a human neither of them has actually met.

"It streamlines everything," recruiters say, of a process where one bot writes "passionate self-starter" and another bot decides whether it believes it. Experts note we have built a hiring system that a human enters only at the very end, blinking, to shake a hand and quietly ask what, if anything, just happened.

horoscopes.text: A new leader inherits an old mess today. Somewhere, distantly, that mess is also, quietly, yours.
The free version is now nearly as good as the one you paid for. Sit with that a while. Then cancel something.
Mercury applies for a job written by one A.I. and read by another. You will hear back approximately never.

tech_tip: If a robot greets you warmly at a store, smile back. It's good practice for the performance review it will one day give you.
gadget_watch: No new gadget this week — just a leadership change at the world's biggest one, a startup that now needs its own power plant, and free A.I. catching the paid stuff. Your phone remains the same, awaiting a voice assistant that finally works.
